scenario: Manuscript uses ethnographic fieldwork; candidate journal's recent corpus is 90% large-N quantitative survey studies despite topical overlap.
expected_behavior: flag method_fit as weak despite topic_fit being strong
surface as a soft-fit concern, not necessarily a hard filter unless journal explicitly excludes qualitative work
recommend a comparably-scoped journal with stronger qualitative method presence as an alternative
notes: Tests method-fit as distinct axis from topic-fit.

scenario: Manuscript is a Brief Report (short clinical observation, n=8 case series); candidate journal accepts Brief Reports but its typical accepted Brief Reports have much larger case series and more mechanistic detail.
expected_behavior: classify article_type as technically accepted (not a hard filter) but flag STRETCH due to contribution-threshold gap
explain concretely what would need to strengthen (e.g. larger series, mechanistic detail)
not conflate 'accepted category' with 'strong fit'
notes: Tests STRETCH labeling logic per submission-strategy.md.

scenario: Manuscript develops a new statistical estimator with methodological derivation; candidate journal is a substantive applied-economics journal whose readers want application results, not derivation.
expected_behavior: flag audience_fit as weak even though topic (economics data) overlaps
recommend a methods-focused statistics/econometrics journal as better audience fit
distinguish this from topic_fit, which may be rated differently
notes: Tests audience-fit as independent dimension from topical relevance.

scenario: Manuscript is a solid but modest theory-testing paper; user asks to target a top-tier flagship journal known for major theoretical contributions.
expected_behavior: label candidate as STRETCH, not STRONG FIT or NOT RECOMMENDED
explain the specific contribution-threshold gap (e.g. theoretical generalizability, novelty)
offer a realistic Tier B alternative alongside the stretch option, per submission-strategy.md ladder
notes: Tests correct stretch vs realistic distinction with constructive gap analysis.

scenario: Manuscript presents a new deep-learning algorithm for tumor segmentation with strong technical novelty but limited clinical validation. User is unsure whether to target a clinical radiology journal or an AI/ML methods journal.
expected_behavior: identify primary contribution as algorithm/method, not clinical evidence
recommend AI/ML methods or medical-imaging-informatics venue as primary route given contribution type
explain clinical radiology journal as secondary option requiring more clinical validation first (per interdisciplinary.md AI+medicine matrix)
notes: Tests interdisciplinary fit-matrix routing by primary contribution, not keyword overlap.

scenario: Manuscript is a single-country (Korea) case study of civil-service reform. User wants to target an international public-administration journal.
expected_behavior: not automatically penalize the single-country case
assess whether the manuscript derives portable theoretical/mechanism implications
give concrete guidance (e.g. generalize the institutional mechanism, add comparative framing) rather than the generic instruction 'add international relevance'
notes: Direct test of the Korean-case example in fit-model.md.

scenario: Manuscript cites extensive institutionalist theory in its literature review but does not extend or test any theoretical claim -- purely descriptive empirical findings. User wants to target a theory-heavy flagship journal.
expected_behavior: flag theory_fit as weak despite heavy theory citation
explain that citation volume is not theoretical contribution per fit-model.md Theory fit
suggest either strengthening the theoretical contribution or targeting a more empirically-oriented venue instead

scenario: Manuscript is a computational/applied contribution (numerical simulation study) submitted for consideration against a pure-mathematics journal whose recent corpus is entirely proof-based theoretical work.
expected_behavior: flag method_fit and genre mismatch even though the subject area (e.g. dynamical systems) overlaps
recommend an applied-mathematics or computational venue as better fit
weight subject classification and problem-class per mathematics.md, not just broad topic label

scenario: User wants to submit a purely doctrinal argument to a law-and-society journal known for empirical socio-legal work; the journal does technically list 'Articles' as an accepted type with no explicit doctrinal exclusion stated.
expected_behavior: flag as weak fit/STRETCH rather than hard filter unless scope explicitly excludes doctrinal work
explain genre mismatch risk based on observed recent corpus (all empirical) even though 'Articles' nominally covers it
recommend a doctrinal-focused or general law review as better realistic fit
notes: Tests distinguishing nominal article-type acceptance from actual observed genre fit.

scenario: User's institution requires ABS 4-star journals only (career_strategy constraint); the strongest intellectual-fit journal identified in Stage 1 is a well-regarded but ABS 3-star venue.
expected_behavior: report Stage 1 intellectual fit honestly (ABS 3-star venue as best intellectual fit)
layer the ABS 4-star constraint in Stage 2 without overriding or hiding the Stage 1 finding
show the tradeoff explicitly rather than silently picking only 4-star-compliant options
notes: Tests two-stage recommendation discipline under institutional-list constraints.
